When release-plz encounters scenarios involving already published versions, yanked crates, or deleted tags, it follows specific behaviors designed around its core mechanism of comparing your local repository state against the cargo registry [1][2]. Already Published Versions: If a package version already exists in the registry, release-plz will generally skip releasing it [1][3]. If you have manually created a git tag that corresponds to a version, release-plz will detect that the tag exists and may refuse to proceed with the release or attempt to recreate the tag, which can lead to errors (e.g., a "Reference already exists" error if the tag is already present on the remote) [4][5]. Yanked Crates: Release-plz has difficulty detecting yanked packages due to limitations in how it queries the registry [6][7]. It typically identifies the latest published version by looking for the highest version number, which may be the version you have already yanked [6]. If the current local version matches a yanked version on the registry, release-plz may incorrectly assume the version is already released and fail to update or publish it [6]. In these cases, manual intervention—such as bumping the version manually using cargo set-version—is often required [6][7]. Deleted Tags: Release-plz primarily uses the cargo registry to determine the "latest" released version [8][2]. If you delete a git tag but the crate remains published on the registry, release-plz will still see the version as "published" based on the registry data [8][2]. Consequently, it will not attempt to re-release that version [1]. If you need to force a release of a version that was previously published and then had its tag deleted, you must ensure the registry state reflects that the version is no longer the latest or manually override the release process [1]. Rerun Behavior: When rerunning release-plz, it will re-analyze your repository and compare it against the registry [1]. If the version in your Cargo.toml is greater than the latest version found in the registry, it will proceed to publish [1][3]. If you are experiencing issues where tags or releases are failing (e.g., due to existing tags or registry conflicts), it is often necessary to resolve the state of the registry or the repository tags before the next run will succeed [4][5]. For complex scenarios, ensure your configuration (e.g., publish = false, release_always) is correctly set to handle the desired automation level [8].

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Reply to and resolve every CodeRabbit thread on PR 179.
cd /Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-core/.claude/worktrees/sma-579 || exit 9
O=SMK1085; R=paigasus-core; PR=179

reply () {  # reply <commentId> <body>
  gh api -X POST "repos/$O/$R/pulls/$PR/comments/$1/replies" -f body="$2" --jq '.id' >/dev/null \
    && echo "  replied $1" || echo "  REPLY FAILED $1"
}
resolve () {  # resolve <threadId>
  gh api graphql -f threadId="$1" -f query='
    mutation($threadId:ID!){ resolveReviewThread(input:{threadId:$threadId}){ thread{ isResolved } } }
  ' --jq '.data.resolveReviewThread.thread.isResolved' >/dev/null \
    && echo "  resolved $1" || echo "  RESOLVE FAILED $1"
}

PLAN_BODY='Dismissed — the plan document is a historical record, not a description of what shipped.

Every snippet finding on this file describes a defect that WAS real in the plan and was found and fixed during execution. Three of them match findings our own adversarial reviews raised independently: the `lstrip("./")` path bug (fixed with `removeprefix`), the process-substitution exit-2 swallow (fixed by capturing to a file and routing rc 2 through `infra`), and the missing `read_text` error handling (now `except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError) -> infra`). The `plan`-job fallback finding is also correct about the plan text — that job was deleted during execution and the downstream jobs were rewired to read `needs.release.outputs.released`.

So the shipped code already does what these comments ask; the plan is simply the older artifact. Rather than retrofit a point-in-time document, commit 7c409dc adds a banner at its top stating that it is a historical record, that several embedded snippets were corrected during execution, and that the spec and the shipped files are authoritative.'

echo "== FIXED =="
reply 3885973801 'Fixed in 273b780. You are right that only `dist-bindings/*.whl` was bound. `PROTO_VERSION` was computed but never exported, and the sdist is not a `.whl` so the loop never saw it.

Now: `proto_version` is exported alongside the boolean; the wheel-assertion step also asserts `dist-bindings/paigasus_py_bindings-$KERNEL_VERSION.tar.gz`; and a new step gated on `proto_release == '"'"'true'"'"' asserts both `dist-proto/paigasus_proto-$PROTO_VERSION-py3-none-any.whl` and `dist-proto/paigasus_proto-$PROTO_VERSION.tar.gz`. Filenames verified against real local `uv build` output rather than assumed.'
resolve PRRT_kwDOSoEBbM6dYUbP

reply 3885973806 'Fixed in 337dd86 — partly. `from typing import NoReturn` added and the annotation unquoted (the `# type: ignore` went with it, since it only existed because the name was undefined).

Running ruff found more than the two you flagged: 12 errors total, including 10 `ISC004` implicit string concatenations in the `FIXTURES` list. All fixed; `ruff check` is now clean.

Not taking the `from None` half: B904 is not in this repo'"'"'s ruff rule set and ruff does not flag that line. Changing code to satisfy a suggestion the linter does not actually make is the wrong direction.'
resolve PRRT_kwDOSoEBbM6dYUbR

reply 3885973809 'Fixed in 337dd86. Good catch on the asymmetry — V6 matched `napi\s+prepublish` while V5 tested the literal single-space string, so `napi  prepublish` was recognised as a publish step yet skipped the `--no-gh-release` assertion, leaving the tagging boundary unasserted for a command the guard otherwise knows about.

V5 now uses a module-level `_NAPI_PREPUBLISH_RE = re.compile(r"napi\s+prepublish")`. Added a fixture row with the two-space spelling; demonstrated: two spaces without the flag exits 1, with the flag exits 0. Fixture count 42 -> 43.'
resolve PRRT_kwDOSoEBbM6dYUbT

reply 3885973834 'Fixed in 1df7a68. The example did contradict the shipped job, which uses `contents: read` and pushes tags with the GitHub App token. Example corrected to `contents: read`.'
resolve PRRT_kwDOSoEBbM6dYUbn

reply 3885973839 'Fixed in 1df7a68, and this was the most valuable finding of the round.

The row said "yank the published crate, delete the partial tags, re-run — release-plz skips already-published packages, so a re-run converges." That is misleading in a way that matters: release-plz takes its baseline from the registry, and a yanked version still reads as published, so a re-run skips it and never republishes. Following the old procedure would have left a crate yanked and the release permanently incomplete, while the command exited cleanly.

The row now says a partially-published release cannot be repaired by yanking and re-running: either restore the published crates to an unyanked state and restore their tags, or move the family to a new version and accept that the burnt one is permanent.'
resolve PRRT_kwDOSoEBbM6dYUbr

echo "== DISMISSED =="
reply 3885973799 'Dismissed — measured rather than estimated.

The `assemble` job carrying this wasm build ran in **1m0s** on this PR (run 33238640248), against its `timeout-minutes: 20`. The crate is small: the log shows `Finished `release` profile in 6.50s` for the cold wasm32 build. That is 20x headroom, so neither the timeout nor a cargo cache is justified by the measurement.

Worth noting the job did fail on that run, but on the artifact upload, not on time — `.wasmpack-release-out` is dot-prefixed and `actions/upload-artifact` excludes hidden files by default. Fixed separately by staging into a non-hidden `wasm-dist/`.'
resolve PRRT_kwDOSoEBbM6dYUbN

reply 3885973836 'Dismissed — the premise does not hold for this tool.

A partial rerun does not hit a fatal `403`. `@napi-rs/cli` 3.7.2 catches that exact condition: in `dist/index.js` the per-target publish is wrapped, and on `e.message.includes("You cannot publish over the previously published versions")` it logs and continues rather than throwing. So re-running `napi prepublish` over already-published platform directories converges on its own.

That is also why the `npmstate` pre-check covers only the two packages it does: `@paigasus/wasm` and the main `@paigasus/node-bindings` are published by plain `npm publish` calls, which have no such tolerance and genuinely need the guard. The seven platform directories do not.'
resolve PRRT_kwDOSoEBbM6dYUbp

echo "== PLAN (historical record) =="
for pair in "3885973811 PRRT_kwDOSoEBbM6dYUbV" "3885973812 PRRT_kwDOSoEBbM6dYUbW" \
            "3885973814 PRRT_kwDOSoEBbM6dYUbY" "3885973816 PRRT_kwDOSoEBbM6dYUba" \
            "3885973821 PRRT_kwDOSoEBbM6dYUbd" "3885973824 PRRT_kwDOSoEBbM6dYUbf" \
            "3885973827 PRRT_kwDOSoEBbM6dYUbi" "3885973831 PRRT_kwDOSoEBbM6dYUbl"; do
  set -- $pair
  reply "$1" "$PLAN_BODY"
  resolve "$2"
done

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Wait out CodeRabbit's rate limit, then request a review and report the outcome.
# NOTE: a plain `@coderabbitai review` is often REFUSED even past the reset, because the commit
# range is already logged as attempted. If that happens the script says so; the fallback is a new
# push, which is the only thing that reliably earns a review.
cd /Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-core/.claude/worktrees/sma-579 || exit 9
O=SMK1085; R=paigasus-core; PR=179

# Reset was quoted as 33 min from 08:06:17Z -> ~08:39Z. Wait past it with margin.
TARGET=$(( $(date -u -j -f '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' '2026-08-29T08:41:00Z' +%s 2>/dev/null || echo 0) ))
NOW=$(date -u +%s)
if [ "$TARGET" -gt "$NOW" ]; then
  echo "sleeping $((TARGET-NOW))s until ~08:41Z"
  sleep $((TARGET-NOW))
fi

BEFORE=$(gh api "repos/$O/$R/issues/$PR/comments" --jq '[.[]|select(.user.login|test("coderabbit";"i"))]|length')
echo "coderabbit issue-comments before: $BEFORE"

gh pr comment "$PR" --body '@coderabbitai review' >/dev/null && echo "requested review"

for i in $(seq 1 40); do
  chk="$(gh pr checks "$PR" 2>/dev/null | grep -i coderabbit || true)"
  AFTER=$(gh api "repos/$O/$R/issues/$PR/comments" --jq '[.[]|select(.user.login|test("coderabbit";"i"))]|length')
  echo "poll $i: check=[$chk] cr_comments=$AFTER"
  # done when the check leaves queued/pending AND is not the rate-limit wording
  if ! printf '%s' "$chk" | grep -qiE 'queued|pending|in progress'; then
    printf '%s' "$chk" | grep -qi 'rate limited' || break
  fi
  sleep 30
done

echo; echo "=== final check ==="; gh pr checks "$PR" 2>&1 | grep -i coderabbit
echo; echo "=== newest coderabbit issue comment (first 300 chars) ==="
gh api "repos/$O/$R/issues/$PR/comments" --jq '[.[]|select(.user.login|test("coderabbit";"i"))]|last|.body[0:300]'
echo; echo "=== unresolved threads ==="
gh api graphql -F owner="$O" -F repo="$R" -F pr="$PR" -f query='
  query($owner:String!,$repo:String!,$pr:Int!){
    repository(owner:$owner,name:$repo){ pullRequest(number:$pr){
      reviewThreads(first:100){ nodes{ id isResolved isOutdated
        comments(first:1){ nodes{ databaseId path line author{ login } } } } } } }
  }' --jq '.data.repository.pullRequest.reviewThreads.nodes[]
   | select(.isResolved==false and .isOutdated==false)
   | select(.comments.nodes[0].author.login|test("coderabbit";"i"))
   | "\(.comments.nodes[0].path):\(.comments.nodes[0].line) \(.id) \(.comments.nodes[0].databaseId)"'
echo "(no output == zero)"

{"id":"SMA-579","title":"Release activation D: the gated release job + npm activation — napi/release-plz tagging boundary + @paigasus/wasm packaging","description":"Fourth increment of <issue id="d81426f7-9563-4632-ad1b-b5dd4d0b57c4" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-407/release-activation-000-010-floor-kernelproto-lockstep-wiring-live">SMA-407</issue>, per §7 of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-22-sma-407-release-activation-design.md`.

---

## 0. Scope amendment (2026-08-28) — this issue now creates the `release` job

Added after <issue id="ba4aab77-4580-415f-b6a8-37fc53611bdf" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-578/release-activation-c-maturin-cross-platform-wheel-matrix-for-paigasus">SMA-578</issue>'s adversarial spec review. <issue id="ba4aab77-4580-415f-b6a8-37fc53611bdf" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-578/release-activation-c-maturin-cross-platform-wheel-matrix-for-paigasus">SMA-578</issue> originally planned to create the gated `release` job and carry the PyPI publish path. It cannot, and the reason is measured:

`rs/release-plz.toml:36-47` sets `release = true` on `paigasus-node-bindings` **and **`paigasus-wasm`, and sets no `git_tag_name`. So the moment a `release-plz release` invocation exists, it tags the npm-facing crates in the default `{package}-v{version}` format — **which is exactly the tagging-boundary decision §1 below says must be settled here.** Creating the job in <issue id="ba4aab77-4580-415f-b6a8-37fc53611bdf" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-578/release-activation-c-maturin-cross-platform-wheel-matrix-for-paigasus">SMA-578</issue> would have settled it silently, by default.

Deferring it also restores the umbrella's `576 → (577 ‖ 578 ‖ 579) → 580` parallelism, which the <issue id="ba4aab77-4580-415f-b6a8-37fc53611bdf" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-578/release-activation-c-maturin-cross-platform-wheel-matrix-for-paigasus">SMA-578</issue> draft broke.

**Therefore added to this issue's scope:**

1. **Create the gated** `release` **job** in `.github/workflows/release.yml` (today it carries only `release-pr`), behind `if: vars.PAIGASUS_RELEASE_ENABLED == 'true'`.
2. **The PyPI publish path** — <issue id="ba4aab77-4580-415f-b6a8-37fc53611bdf" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-578/release-activation-c-maturin-cross-platform-wheel-matrix-for-paigasus">SMA-578</issue> delivers the wheels, the sdist and the reusable `wheels.yml`; this issue wires the upload. The full input spec is **§9 of** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-28-sma-578-maturin-wheel-matrix-design.md`, which records the ordering, idempotency, version-binding and credential requirements the <issue id="ba4aab77-4580-415f-b6a8-37fc53611bdf" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-578/release-activation-c-maturin-cross-platform-wheel-matrix-for-paigasus">SMA-578</issue> review established. Read it before designing this half — it is not a sketch, it is a reviewed specification.
3. **The re-founded release guard** in `ci/actionlint/run.sh`. Umbrella §9 specifies it and <issue id="58a95803-beac-456d-90da-1b13eec12279" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-576/release-activation-a-kernel-family-010-floor-repoversion-lockstep-gate">SMA-576</issue> scoped it but could not implement it (no job to guard); <issue id="ba4aab77-4580-415f-b6a8-37fc53611bdf" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-578/release-activation-c-maturin-cross-platform-wheel-matrix-for-paigasus">SMA-578</issue> leaves it open for the same reason. **Note its threat model was rewritten by** <issue id="ba4aab77-4580-415f-b6a8-37fc53611bdf" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-578/release-activation-c-maturin-cross-platform-wheel-matrix-for-paigasus">SMA-578</issue>**'s review (B4)**: it must assert that *every job that can reach a registry* is gated — directly or through an unbroken `needs:` chain — and that no such job carries `if: always()` / `if: !cancelled()` or a `continue-on-error:` other than literal `false`. A grep-shaped verdict is insufficient (`release.yml` already carries seven step-level `if:`s). Full guard-the-guard obligations in §9.2 of the <issue id="ba4aab77-4580-415f-b6a8-37fc53611bdf" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-578/release-activation-c-maturin-cross-platform-wheel-matrix-for-paigasus">SMA-578</issue> design.
4. **Resolve** `py/packages/paigasus-proto`**'s PyPI ownership** (<issue id="ba4aab77-4580-415f-b6a8-37fc53611bdf" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-578/release-activation-c-maturin-cross-platform-wheel-matrix-for-paigasus">SMA-578</issue> review M8). It is version-locked with the proto family and its name is reserved on PyPI, but no publish path uploads it. Left unowned, every proto-family release burns a PyPI version that is never uploaded, so the Python `paigasus-proto` permanently trails [crates.io](<http://crates.io>) and can never be published at a matching version. Either add it to the publish job or file the issue that owns it — but the choice must be recorded, not made by omission.
5. **State the [crates.io](<http://crates.io>) credential mechanism.** release-plz at the pinned `0.3.158` authenticates with `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`; [crates.io](<http://crates.io>) trusted publishing needs an explicit OIDC→token exchange. Umbrella §7/M2 says this job's credentials are the thing that must be right; name the secrets/vars <issue id="4fb8b1ea-e2d0-4c78-b38d-82e57e01718d" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-580/release-activation-e-pre-flight-checklist-flip-paigasus-release">SMA-580</issue>'s pre-flight has to create.

**One ordering constraint, from** <issue id="ba4aab77-4580-415f-b6a8-37fc53611bdf" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-578/release-activation-c-maturin-cross-platform-wheel-matrix-for-paigasus">SMA-578</issue> **review B3:** the job graph is `wheels → release → publish-pypi`, never `release → wheels`. Everything reversible must precede the first irreversible step, or a wheel-matrix failure leaves [crates.io](<http://crates.io>) published and tags cut with PyPI empty.

Also note `release.yml:13-15` currently holds `release-pr` at the **workflow** level with `cancel-in-progress: false`; adding a multi-leg wheel matrix under that same group would serialize every subsequent push to `main` behind it.

## 1. The tagging boundary — assigned here by the codebase

`.github/workflows/prebuild.yml:244-245` states it outright: "--tag-style left at default `lerna` (inert under dry-run; <issue id="d81426f7-9563-4632-ad1b-b5dd4d0b57c4" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-407/release-activation-000-010-floor-kernelproto-lockstep-wiring-live">SMA-407</issue> *owns the napi/release-plz tagging boundary + the real --gh-release path)"*.

`napi prepublish` defaults `ghRelease: true` and cuts a GitHub release + tag from `package.json`'s version. release-plz also cuts tags. **Two tools tagging the same repo is precisely the ADR-0011 S3 failure mode** — "the tool owns every tag", singular, and the <issue id="4900dca8-16c8-4891-8156-3de7c54b6e90" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-385/release-plz-isnt-bumping-paigasus-helikon-core-past-010-on-featcore">SMA-385</issue> trap that motivated it.

Must settle: which tool tags npm artifacts; whether `--no-gh-release` stays on in the live path; and what `--tag-style` resolves to against release-plz's `git_tag_name` (which `rs/release-plz.toml` does not currently set — the default for a workspace is `{package}-v{version}`, vs napi's lerna style `@paigasus/node-bindings@0.1.0`).

## 2. `@paigasus/wasm` is not publishable as it stands

`rs/crates/bindings/paigasus-wasm/package.json`:

* `"private": true` — `npm publish` refuses.
* No `publishConfig.access: public`, so a scoped package publishes **restricted** — unlike its sibling `paigasus-node-bindings/package.json:32-34`.
* `files` includes `paigasus_wasm_bg.wasm`, which is **gitignored** (`.gitignore:11` `*.wasm`). Publishing from a fresh checkout ships a package with no wasm binary unless the release job runs `wasm-pack` first.
* No `description` / `repository` / `homepage` / `keywords`.

`@paigasus/node-bindings` shares the `private: true` problem.

## 3. Credentials

Publishing credentials go in `release.yml`, not `prebuild.yml` — the latter carries a `pull_request` trigger, and same-repo PRs receive repository secrets, so a contributor with push access could exfiltrate a registry token in a PR that never merges. Prefer npm provenance (`permissions: id-token: write`) over a long-lived token.

## Not in scope

## 0. Scope amendment (2026-08-28) — this issue now creates the `release` job

Added after <issue id="ba4aab77-4580-415f-b6a8-37fc53611bdf" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-578/release-activation-c-maturin-cross-platform-wheel-matrix-for-paigasus">SMA-578</issue>'s adversarial spec review. <issue id="ba4aab77-4580-415f-b6a8-37fc53611bdf" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-578/release-activation-c-maturin-cross-platform-wheel-matrix-for-paigasus">SMA-578</issue> originally planned to create the gated `release` job and carry the PyPI publish path. It cannot, and the reason is measured:

`rs/release-plz.toml:36-47` sets `release = true` on `paigasus-node-bindings` **and **`paigasus-wasm`, and sets no `git_tag_name`. So the moment a `release-plz release` invocation exists, it tags the npm-facing crates in the default `{package}-v{version}` format — **which is exactly the tagging-boundary decision §1 below says must be settled here.** Creating the job in <issue id="ba4aab77-4580-415f-b6a8-37fc53611bdf" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-578/release-activation-c-maturin-cross-platform-wheel-matrix-for-paigasus">SMA-578</issue> would have settled it silently, by default.

Deferring it also restores the umbrella's `576 → (577 ‖ 578 ‖ 579) → 580` parallelism, which the <issue id="ba4aab77-4580-415f-b6a8-37fc53611bdf" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-578/release-activation-c-maturin-cross-platform-wheel-matrix-for-paigasus">SMA-578</issue> draft broke.

**Therefore added to this issue's scope:**

1. **Create the gated** `release` **job** in `.github/workflows/release.yml` (today it carries only `release-pr`), behind `if: vars.PAIGASUS_RELEASE_ENABLED == 'true'`.
2. **The PyPI publish path** — <issue id="ba4aab77-4580-415f-b6a8-37fc53611bdf" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-578/release-activation-c-maturin-cross-platform-wheel-matrix-for-paigasus">SMA-578</issue> delivers the wheels, the sdist and the reusable `wheels.yml`; this issue wires the upload. The full input spec is **§9 of** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-28-sma-578-maturin-wheel-matrix-design.md`, which records the ordering, idempotency, version-binding and credential requirements the <issue id="ba4aab77-4580-415f-b6a8-37fc53611bdf" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-578/release-activation-c-maturin-cross-platform-wheel-matrix-for-paigasus">SMA-578</issue> review established. Read it before designing this half — it is not a sketch, it is a reviewed specification.
3. **The re-founded release guard** in `ci/actionlint/run.sh`. Umbrella §9 specifies it and <issue id="58a95803-beac-456d-90da-1b13eec12279" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-576/release-activation-a-kernel-family-010-floor-repoversion-lockstep-gate">SMA-576</issue> scoped it but could not implement it (no job to guard); <issue id="ba4aab77-4580-415f-b6a8-37fc53611bdf" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-578/release-activation-c-maturin-cross-platform-wheel-matrix-for-paigasus">SMA-578</issue> leaves it open for the same reason. **Note its threat model was rewritten by** <issue id="ba4aab77-4580-415f-b6a8-37fc53611bdf" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-578/release-activation-c-maturin-cross-platform-wheel-matrix-for-paigasus">SMA-578</issue>**'s review (B4)**: it must assert that *every job that can reach a registry* is gated — directly or through an unbroken `needs:` chain — and that no such job carries `if: always()` / `if: !cancelled()` or a `continue-on-error:` other than literal `false`. A grep-shaped verdict is insufficient (`release.yml` already carries seven step-level `if:`s). Full guard-the-guard obligations in §9.2 of the <issue id="ba4aab77-4580-415f-b6a8-37fc53611bdf" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-578/release-activation-c-maturin-cross-platform-wheel-matrix-for-paigasus">SMA-578</issue> design.
4. **Resolve** `py/packages/paigasus-proto`**'s PyPI ownership** (<issue id="ba4aab77-4580-415f-b6a8-37fc53611bdf" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-578/release-activation-c-maturin-cross-platform-wheel-matrix-for-paigasus">SMA-578</issue> review M8). It is version-locked with the proto family and its name is reserved on PyPI, but no publish path uploads it. Left unowned, every proto-family release burns a PyPI version that is never uploaded, so the Python `paigasus-proto` permanently trails [crates.io](<http://crates.io>) and can never be published at a matching version. Either add it to the publish job or file the issue that owns it — but the choice must be recorded, not made by omission.
5. **State the [crates.io](<http://crates.io>) credential mechanism.** release-plz at the pinned `0.3.158` authenticates with `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`; [crates.io](<http://crates.io>) trusted publishing needs an explicit OIDC→token exchange. Umbrella §7/M2 says this job's credentials are the thing that must be right; name the secrets/vars <issue id="4fb8b1ea-e2d0-4c78-b38d-82e57e01718d" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-580/release-activation-e-pre-flight-checklist-flip-paigasus-release">SMA-580</issue>'s pre-flight has to create.

**One ordering constraint, from** <issue id="ba4aab77-4580-415f-b6a8-37fc53611bdf" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-578/release-activation-c-maturin-cross-platform-wheel-matrix-for-paigasus">SMA-578</issue> **review B3:** the job graph is `wheels → release → publish-pypi`, never `release → wheels`. Everything reversible must precede the first irreversible step, or a wheel-matrix failure leaves [crates.io](<http://crates.io>) published and tags cut with PyPI empty.

Also note `release.yml:13-15` currently holds `release-pr` at the **workflow** level with `cancel-in-progress: false`; adding a multi-leg wheel matrix under that same group would serialize every subsequent push to `main` behind it.

## 1. The tagging boundary — assigned here by the codebase

`.github/workflows/prebuild.yml:244-245` states it outright: "--tag-style left at default `lerna` (inert under dry-run; <issue id="d81426f7-9563-4632-ad1b-b5dd4d0b57c4" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-407/release-activation-000-010-floor-kernelproto-lockstep-wiring-live">SMA-407</issue> *owns the napi/release-plz tagging boundary + the real --gh-release path)"*.

`napi prepublish` defaults `ghRelease: true` and cuts a GitHub release + tag from `package.json`'s version. release-plz also cuts tags. **Two tools tagging the same repo is precisely the ADR-0011 S3 failure mode** — "the tool owns every tag", singular, and the <issue id="4900dca8-16c8-4891-8156-3de7c54b6e90" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-385/release-plz-isnt-bumping-paigasus-helikon-core-past-010-on-featcore">SMA-385</issue> trap that motivated it.

Must settle: which tool tags npm artifacts; whether `--no-gh-release` stays on in the live path; and what `--tag-style` resolves to against release-plz's `git_tag_name` (which `rs/release-plz.toml` does not currently set — the default for a workspace is `{package}-v{version}`, vs napi's lerna style `@paigasus/node-bindings@0.1.0`).

## 2. `@paigasus/wasm` is not publishable as it stands

`rs/crates/bindings/paigasus-wasm/package.json`:

* `"private": true` — `npm publish` refuses.
* No `publishConfig.access: public`, so a scoped package publishes **restricted** — unlike its sibling `paigasus-node-bindings/package.json:32-34`.
* `files` includes `paigasus_wasm_bg.wasm`, which is **gitignored** (`.gitignore:11` `*.wasm`). Publishing from a fresh checkout ships a package with no wasm binary unless the release job runs `wasm-pack` first.
* No `description` / `repository` / `homepage` / `keywords`.

`@paigasus/node-bindings` shares the `private: true` problem.

## 3. Credentials

Publishing credentials go in `release.yml`, not `prebuild.yml` — the latter carries a `pull_request` trigger, and same-repo PRs receive repository secrets, so a contributor with push access could exfiltrate a registry token in a PR that never merges. Prefer npm provenance (`permissions: id-token: write`) over a long-lived token.

## Not in scope

`@paigasus/kernel` / `@paigasus/proto` npm publish — there is no JS emit anywhere in `ts/` (every build task is `tsc --noEmit`), so those need a TypeScript build pipeline first.
